text: Take two phones, identical in every way.
on_screen_event: two phones drawn white on the balance pans

text: Charge one completely, drain the other until it's dead,
visual_cue: battery glyphs on screens: full / empty
on_screen_event: coral block fills the left phone's battery

text: and set them on a balance.
on_screen_event: balance drawn around the phones

text: The charged phone is heavier.
on_screen_event: punch-in: exaggerated tilt wedge on the left pan

text: Not by any amount you could measure.
visual_cue: tiny question mark by the tilt
on_screen_event: note: 'heavier by ???'

text: Yet nothing material went in while it charged.
on_screen_event: charging cable drawn to the left phone

text: No atoms came down the cable.
on_screen_event: note: '0 atoms in'

text: No extra electrons piled up either: every electron that flowed in through one wire flowed back out through the other.
on_screen_event: electron loop arrows along the cable

text: The only thing the phone gained was energy.
visual_cue: energy block glows into the battery
on_screen_event: colour flood: coral ENERGY block enters the phone

text: And energy, it turns out, has weight.
visual_cue: the coral block sits on the pan
on_screen_event: the energy block becomes the mystery; chapter capsule

text: Inside the battery, charging doesn't add stuff. It rearranges it.
on_screen_event: battery cross-section drawn (holes as layers)

text: Ions shuttle between two layers into an arrangement that stores energy, like a stretched spring.
on_screen_event: ions + arrows between the two electrode layers

text: Use the phone, and they slide back down, releasing it.
on_screen_event: discharge arrows (grey) opposite the coral charge arrows

text: A full battery and an empty one hold exactly the same atoms.
on_screen_event: note: 'same atoms, same electrons'

text: The only difference is energy.
on_screen_event: swatch strip states tracked

text: So why would energy have weight at all?
on_screen_event: camera drifts up; the question written large

text: Matter is supposed to be the thing that weighs.
on_screen_event: half-coloured block left; transition drift right

text: For a century, science's most careful weighings said the opposite:
on_screen_event: new region: 1770s Paris lab table

text: nothing inside a sealed container can change its weight.
on_screen_event: sealed glass vessel with tin block inside

text: The rule was born in Paris, in the seventeen seventies, with Antoine Lavoisier, a chemist who trusted his balance more than any theory.
on_screen_event: handwritten label + leader line

text: He sealed tin inside a glass vessel, melting the glass shut so nothing could get in or out, and took its weight.
on_screen_event: vessel neck sealed; note written

text: Then he heated it, until part of the shiny metal turned to grey powder, let it cool, and took its weight again.
on_screen_event: flame + mustard heat waves through the glass

text: Heat had poured in and out. The weight had not changed at all.
on_screen_event: both balance readings match; coral 'unchanged!'

text: In seventeen eighty-nine, his rule: an equal quantity of matter, before and after.
on_screen_event: note card: the conservation rule, coral underline

text: Energy, it seemed, weighs nothing.
on_screen_event: swatch strip: 'energy weighs nothing?'

text: But a rule is only as good as the balance that tests it.
on_screen_event: new region: Berlin, 1890s

text: In the eighteen nineties, Hans Landolt in Berlin spent twenty years testing it harder than anyone.
on_screen_event: label + two-decade calendar note

text: Two chemicals, sealed in the separate arms of a glass vessel, react;
on_screen_event: H-vessel drawn; coral + mustard chemicals in the arms

text: the heat escapes; he weighs it again. And again. And again.
on_screen_event: colour flood: chemicals merge mottled; heat arrows rise; weigh ticks

text: He chased every error — buoyancy, moisture, dust.
on_screen_event: error-hunting list written

text: His nineteen oh eight verdict: no reaction changed weight by more than three hundredths of a milligram.
on_screen_event: punch-in on the needle; coral circle around '0.03 mg'

text: If the escaping heat weighed anything at all, it weighed less than that.
on_screen_event: error bar drawn under the needle

text: Then a tiny glowing sample made that answer hard to believe.
on_screen_event: new region: back in Paris, 1902

text: Radium, which Marie Curie purified in nineteen oh two, from more than a ton of ore.
on_screen_event: purification chain drawn: ton of ore into one vial

text: Pierre Curie measured one gram giving off a hundred calories of heat, every hour.
on_screen_event: heat waves radiate; '100 cal/hour' note

text: That adds up to nearly nine hundred thousand calories a year.
on_screen_event: calendar pages drawn flying; radium bar grows tall (coral)

text: A gram of coal gives seven thousand. Then it's gone.
on_screen_event: coal bar stays tiny (graphite); swatch strip records both

text: The radium releases a hundred times more, every year, and barely slows down:
on_screen_event: coral '×100' bursts between the bars

text: half is still there sixteen hundred years from now.
on_screen_event: decay line drawn; 'half remains at 1,600 years'

text: Nobody could say what it was using up.
on_screen_event: big '?' over the glowing vial

text: Either it soaked up invisible energy from space, or the energy came from inside the atom itself.
on_screen_event: option A: sky-to-vial arrow; option B: atom cross-section

text: The first clue had appeared earlier, in the way light behaves.
on_screen_event: new region: light, 1900

text: In nineteen hundred, Henri Poincaré worked through a fact most people never think about: light pushes.
on_screen_event: sun + radiating light rays drawn

text: It's why a comet's tail points away from the Sun;
on_screen_event: comet + tail pushed outward

text: and lab experiments had just measured that push.
on_screen_event: light-pressure apparatus: beam pushing a vane

text: Anything that pushes carries momentum.
on_screen_event: note: 'push = momentum'

text: A flash of energy E carries momentum: E divided by the speed of light.
on_screen_event: handwritten: 'momentum = E / c'

text: Momentum is mass times speed.
on_screen_event: handwritten: 'momentum = mass × speed'

text: What mass would that flash need? Its energy, divided by the speed of light squared.
on_screen_event: match cut + punch-in: 'mass = E / c²' in coral

text: His example: a one kilogram lamp firing three million joules of light recoils like a cannon,
on_screen_event: lamp fires a flash; recoil arrow '1 cm/s'

text: while the flash carries thirty-three billionths of a gram.
on_screen_event: flash labelled '33 billionths of a gram'

text: But he called it a fiction, not a real weight.
on_screen_event: 'a fictitious fluid' — quote note beside the number

text: The number sat there. He didn't believe it.
on_screen_event: the coral formula left half-coloured; transition drift

text: Believing it took Albert Einstein — twenty six, a clerk at the patent office in Bern.
on_screen_event: new region: Bern, 1905; desk + patent doodles

text: In nineteen oh five, just after finishing relativity, he wrote to a friend:
on_screen_event: letter card drawn with the claim

text: a body's mass must be a measure of the energy inside it.
on_screen_event: coral underline under the claim

text: Light carries mass, he said. Radium should get noticeably lighter.
on_screen_event: small radium vial with down-arrow

text: That September, three pages in the leading physics journal.
on_screen_event: paper with '3 pages' note

text: A glowing object, at rest, fires two identical flashes in opposite directions.
on_screen_event: glowing dot; two mustard flashes left/right

text: The pushes cancel. It just loses the light's energy, L.
on_screen_event: 'L' labels both flashes; arrows cancel

text: Now watch from a passing train.
on_screen_event: match cut: same drawing, train + motion lines

text: The speed is unchanged, but the forward flash now looks slightly more energetic, the backward slightly less.
on_screen_event: forward flash redrawn longer, backward shorter

text: Add them: most of the difference cancels. Not all.
on_screen_event: energy bookkeeping: 'L + a little extra'

text: From the train, the light carries away a little more than L.
on_screen_event: coral highlight on the extra

text: That extra must come out of its kinetic energy.
on_screen_event: note: 'paid out of kinetic energy'

text: And kinetic energy is one half, times mass, times speed squared.
on_screen_event: handwritten: 'kinetic = ½ · mass · speed²'

text: The speed hasn't changed. So the mass drops —
on_screen_event: 'speed' crossed out; 'mass?' remains

text: by the light's energy, divided by the speed of light squared.
on_screen_event: punch-in: the same coral formula, re-registered solid

text: A year later, Einstein offered a simpler argument: a flash of light inside a box.
on_screen_event: new region: a box floats in space; starfield dots

text: Walk from one end of a small boat to the other, and it slides back under you.
on_screen_event: boat + walking figure; slide arrows

text: Nothing inside a closed system can move its own centre of mass.
on_screen_event: centre-of-mass dot + fixed axis drawn

text: Now make it a box in empty space, and make you a flash of light off the left wall.
on_screen_event: colour flood: the boat block becomes the box

text: The flash pushes the box back, crosses, and is absorbed at the right wall —
on_screen_event: box recoil arrow; flash travels (dashed); absorption burst

text: the box stops, shifted. Nothing outside touched it.
on_screen_event: ruler shows the shift d; note 'nothing outside'

text: So either the box pushed itself through space, or the light carried mass, wall to wall.
on_screen_event: option notes: 'magic push' vs 'light carries mass'

text: The boat settles it: box mass times shift equals light mass times box length.
on_screen_event: handwritten: 'M·d = m·L'

text: Everything cancels but one line: the light's mass equals its energy, divided by the speed of light squared.
on_screen_event: punch-in: 'm = E / c²' in a coral box

text: The left wall really gets lighter. The right wall really gets heavier.
on_screen_event: left wall block fades lighter, right wall heavier

text: Einstein credited Poincaré on the paper's first page.
on_screen_event: note: 'built on Poincaré's reasoning'

text: Once energy has real weight, the old mysteries make sense.
on_screen_event: new region: the fraction

text: Only one thing hid that weight: the size of c squared.
on_screen_event: 'c' written, squared

text: Light moves at three hundred million metres per second.
on_screen_event: handwritten: 'c = 300,000,000 m/s'

text: So c squared is ninety million billion.
Ninety million billion joules, for one kilogram of weight.
on_screen_event: the fraction: tiny E over a huge graphite slab

text: Landolt's escaping heat weighed about a billionth of a gram.
on_screen_event: swatch strip: reaction heat, a billionth g

text: His balance could only see thirty millionths of a gram.
on_screen_event: swatch strip: balance sees 30 millionths g

text: Tens of thousands of times too coarse.
on_screen_event: coral '×30,000 too coarse' between swatches

text: Even a gram of radium radiates a whole year of heat that weighs just forty billionths of a gram,
on_screen_event: capsule drawn; 12-month dial around it

text: right at the edge of the finest balances — after twelve patient months.
on_screen_event: needle drawn a hair off zero; 'a full year' note

text: So could anyone weigh energy at all?
on_screen_event: new region: Cambridge, 1932

text: It would take more energy per atom, and a way to weigh single atoms.
on_screen_event: two notes: 'more energy per atom' / 'weigh single atoms'

text: Both arrived in Rutherford's lab in Cambridge.
on_screen_event: vacuum chamber + magnet poles drawn

text: Atoms were no longer weighed on pans: flying through magnetic fields in a vacuum, the lighter ones curve more sharply. The bend became the scale.
on_screen_event: dashed arcs: light atom bends hard, heavy bends less

text: On the fourteenth of April, nineteen thirty-two, researchers fired fast protons at a thin layer of lithium.
on_screen_event: proton beam from left; thin lithium target

text: One watched from a darkened hut beneath the machine, shielded from X-rays.
on_screen_event: hut drawn under the machine; observer figure inside

text: The screen lit up.
on_screen_event: particle sparkles burst on the screen

text: Rutherford squeezed in: the flashes looked, he said, mighty like alpha particles.
on_screen_event: quote card: 'mighty like alpha particles'

text: A lithium nucleus had swallowed a proton and split into two helium nuclei,
on_screen_event: match cut: magnified reaction; lithium swallows proton

text: flying apart with seventeen point two million electron volts.
on_screen_event: shatter: two alpha particles burst apart with energy arrows

text: Lithium plus hydrogen outweighs two heliums.
on_screen_event: ledger: 'Li + H > He + He'

text: If Einstein was right, the missing mass times c squared must equal that energy.
on_screen_event: coral '=' drawn between missing mass and energy

text: But lithium's nineteen thirty-two mass predicted only fourteen million electron volts, against seventeen.
on_screen_event: bar: predicted 14 vs measured 17.2; 'blurry'

text: A year later, a more precise lithium mass raised the prediction to sixteen point eight — within a few percent. It matched.
on_screen_event: bar re-registered: 16.8 close to 17.2; check mark

text: Weighing atoms had already explained something bigger.
on_screen_event: new region: the stars

text: In nineteen twenty, helium proved lighter than the four hydrogens that build it.
on_screen_event: four pale hydrogen circles drawn

text: Four point zero three one three, against four point zero zero two six.
on_screen_event: handwritten ledger: '4.0313 to 4.0026'

text: Arthur Eddington saw that the missing mass could power the stars.
on_screen_event: small telescope doodle; label 'Eddington, 1920'

text: Fusing hydrogen into helium leaves seven tenths of one percent missing, carried away as energy.
on_screen_event: four H merge into one He; a coral chip flies off

text: The Sun fuses six hundred million tons of hydrogen a second,
on_screen_event: sun with rays; '600,000,000 t/s' note

text: and four million tons of that never becomes matter — it leaves as light.
on_screen_event: rays leave; '4,000,000 t/s' in coral

text: The same equation runs the stars, and the battery in your pocket.
on_screen_event: tiny phone doodle beside the sun; coral link

text: So, back to the phones.
on_screen_event: match cut: the ch1 balance region, aged

text: The charged one gained energy, and therefore mass: less than a billionth of a gram.
visual_cue: phone on the pan, tiny block
on_screen_event: charged phone redrawn; coral energy block on the pan

text: No balance can show it. We know it anyway:
on_screen_event: the tilt wedge again; 'unmeasurable' note

text: every kind of energy weighs exactly its amount, divided by c squared.
on_screen_event: the equation written large, mustard block under 'mc²'

text: Almost all the mass of your body is energy too, locked in its protons and neutrons.
on_screen_event: body outline drawn; match cut: magnifier with a proton

text: The three quarks in a proton are less than one percent of its weight.
on_screen_event: three small dots in the proton; '<1%' note

text: The rest is the strong force — trapped, seething motion.
on_screen_event: colour flood: the proton floods with energy texture

text: You are mostly stored energy, wearing the shape of a person. So is your phone.
on_screen_event: the body and phone blocks re-registered to coral

text: Charge it tonight, and in the morning, it will be ever so slightly heavier.
on_screen_event: camera settles: phone, balance, E = mc²; end card drawn
